key_insight: Latent image information (perceptual and semantic content) is carried mainly by the angular (direction) component of VAE latents that lie on thin spherical shells; aligning flow matching to this spherical geometry (transporting along angular/geodesic directions and treating radius separately) yields more faithful generation than straight Euclidean chords.
problem_solved: Standard latent flow matching transports between Gaussian noise and VAE latents along linear Euclidean paths that cross low-probability regions off the thin spherical shells where latents concentrate, degrading decoded image quality and failing to respect the true geometry of the latent space.
method: Decompose each latent token into radial and angular components and probe their roles via component-swap experiments to show direction dominates semantic/perceptual content.
Align latent geometry by preprocessing and designing flows that match on the sphere (angular/geodesic transport) while handling radius separately, avoiding off-shell Euclidean chords.
Train spherical flow-matching models that follow angular trajectories (e.g., great-circle-like interpolation or spherical vector fields) and verify improved decoding and metrics.
impact: Respecting spherical latent geometry yields more robust and higher-fidelity image generation without major architecture changes—useful for practitioners building VAE+flow generative pipelines or improving existing flow-matching methods. It clarifies where information lives in latents, informing design choices (interpolation, regularization, augmentations).
visual_elements: Diagram of latent shell geometry: thin spherical shells for both endpoints, showing Euclidean chord vs spherical/geodesic path.
Illustration of radial vs angular decomposition with example latents and arrows indicating which component carries perceptual/semantic content.
Component-swap grid: decoded images from swapping radius/angle to show direction preserves identity/content while radius changes style/scale.
Before/after metric chart (e.g., FID/IS) and sample montage comparing Euclidean flow-matching vs spherical-aligned flow-matching.
paper_title: Aligning Latent Geometry for Spherical Flow Matching in Image Generation
paper_authors: Tuna Han Salih Meral, Kaan Oktay, Hidir Yesiltepe, Adil Kaan Akan, Pinar Yanardag
